review_notes: I read the whole target file and the RelativeGroupLaw definitions (Def_AlgebraicGeometry_RelativeGroupLaw.lean, Def_GoodReductionJacobian_RelativeGroupLawKernel.lean) and castOver (Def_ModularCurve_JZeroNeronObjectAtP.lean). I also grepped for duplicated copies of the helper lemmas elsewhere in the repo. The file has no @[simp] declarations of its own, and it mostly uses explicit rw or simp only. The findings are about missing or badly oriented simp lemmas for local helpers. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp loops or failures, and the proposed lemma statements are untested. Some reservations: moving lemmas into the Def files would affect many downstream files, and the one_castOver reorientation depends on the cast lemma's dependent-type behaviour.

findings.excerpt: L.one ι' = castOver h (L.one ι) := by
findings.problem: The cast-handling rules have no usable simp normal form. `one_castOver` rewrites a plain `L.one ι'` into `castOver h (L.one ι)`, which is an expanding direction. Used as a simp lemma it would be non-terminating, because the right-hand side contains `L.one ι` again. `nsmul_castOver` instead pulls `castOver` outward. The two lemmas therefore go in different directions, and the `castOver` projection `(castOver h x).1 = x.1` has no simp lemma either. The only use is a manual `rw [hx, pts_zero, hx', nsmul_castOver, one_castOver O.L Λ.hσA] at h3`, which has to supply the cast proof explicitly and depends on the rewrite order.
findings.proposed_change: State the cast lemmas so that casts are eliminated or pushed outward, and mark them @[simp]. For example, `castOver h (L.one ι) = L.one ι'` (the pull-in direction), plus a rfl lemma `(castOver h x).1 = x.1`. Keep `nsmul_castOver` as the outward-pushing rule. The step at line 206 then becomes a `simp`/`simp only` call that does not depend on the order of the `rw`s. Alternatively, if the expanding form is wanted for `rw`, rename it `one_eq_castOver_one` and state the simp-form lemma separately.
findings.benefit: Casts along equalities of base points become predictable under simp. A reader no longer needs a hand-ordered `rw` chain with explicit proof arguments, and there is no risk of someone tagging the current expanding lemma @[simp].

findings.declaration: FINFIXEDH.inv_one (and the group-law helper family in section grp)
findings.excerpt: theorem inv_one : L.inv t (L.one t) = L.one t :=
findings.problem: `inv_one` is the canonical simp identity for a group law. It is a local, non-simp theorem inside `FINFIXEDH`, not a simp lemma in the `RelativeGroupLaw` namespace. The same statement is re-proved as a private-looking local theorem in other files, for example `inv_one` / `inv_one_pt` in two other Sol files. The core simplifying laws in the Def file (`one_mul`, `mul_one`, `inv_mul_cancel`, `mul_inv_cancel`, `one_natural`, `nsmul_unit`) are also not simp. As a result every use here is an explicit `rw`, for example `rw [nsmul_mul_of_comm O.L _ O.comm, nsmul_inv_of_comm O.L _ O.comm, hs_tors, hs'_tors, inv_one, O.L.one_mul]`.
findings.proposed_change: Move `inv_one` into `NeronModelInfra`/`GoodReductionJacobian.RelativeGroupLaw` next to `mul_inv_cancel` and tag it @[simp]. Tag `RelativeGroupLaw.one_mul`, `mul_one`, `inv_mul_cancel`, `mul_inv_cancel` and `nsmul_unit` @[simp] as well, in the style of Mathlib's `Group` lemmas. They are plain cancellations with no side conditions and each strictly shrinks the term. Then the torsion computation at line 253 can be a `simp [nsmul_mul_of_comm ..., hs_tors, hs'_tors]` call instead of a six-step `rw`.
findings.benefit: One canonical simp-normal form for the pointwise group law. It removes the per-file copies of `inv_one` and the manual rewrite chains. Call sites need only `simp` to cancel units and inverses.

findings.problem: `inv_natural` is the missing naturality companion of `mul_natural`, `one_natural` and `nsmul_natural`. It is proved locally and is not a field or lemma of `RelativeGroupLaw`. The naturality lemmas are not simp either. Compare the structure field `mul_natural` and `one_natural` in the Def file, which carry no @[simp]. The same lemma is re-proved in at least 30 other Sol files (for example `S_AlgebraicGeometry_Polarisation_mapPt_negMor_mul.lean`). Rewriting at line 261 therefore needs `rw [O.L.mul_natural, inv_natural, hred, O.L.mul_inv_cancel, O.L.one_natural]` with every step named by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add `RelativeGroupLaw.inv_natural` next to `one_natural` in the Def file. Tag the naturality family `mul_natural`, `inv_natural`, `one_natural` and `nsmul_natural` @[simp]. All four push `schemeHomOverComp` inward onto the arguments, which is a consistent direction because `schemeHomOverComp_coe` is already simp. Delete the per-file copies.
findings.benefit: A single canonical simp direction, with `schemeHomOverComp` pushed to the leaves. This removes dozens of duplicate lemmas, and calls like the one at line 261 reduce to `simp [hred]`.

findings.problem: `actA` is a new def with no simp lemma saying how it acts on elements (`actA τ a = τ • a`) or on coercions. As a result, proofs reach through the definition with `ext a; rfl` and `show residue ↥A (τ • a) = residue ↥A a` (lines 138 and 162), plus an ad hoc `have h1 : ... := rfl`. These rely on defeq unfolding and bypass the simp set. `actSpec` also has no simp lemma `actSpec τ = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (actA τ))`. Without these lemmas, any later `simp` call stalls on `actA τ a` or `(actA τ a : AlgebraicClosure ℚ)`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem actA_apply (a : ↥A) : actA τ a = τ • a := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem coe_actA (a : ↥A) : (actA τ a : AlgebraicClosure ℚ) = (τ : AlgebraicClosure ℚ ≃ₐ[ℚ] AlgebraicClosure ℚ) a := rfl`. Then `subtype_comp_actA` is `by ext a; simp`, and `residue_comp_actA` reduces to `ext a; simp [h2]` without the `show` and `h1`. Optionally add an `actSpec_def` lemma (`actSpec τ = Spec.map ...`, by rfl) so that `barPt_actSpec` and `resPt_actSpec` can stop using `show Spec.map _ ≫ Spec.map _ = ...`.
findings.benefit: The abstraction boundary of `actA` is documented in simp lemmas. The Galois-action proofs become robust to changes in the definition, and future users get element-wise normalisation instead of having to unfold with `show`.
